thread:
marta: Quick heads-up — after the kernel selector change yesterday I see weird regional cache stats. US has ~52% prefix hit, EU ~18%, APAC ~7%.
igor: ugh. is that after the batching tweak too or just kernel?
marta: both landed in the same deploy window. the perf regression PR included the new kernel heuristics + a small batching tweak that lowers max batch wait.
deepa: can you paste the exact metric names/queries? I want to rule out a dashboard mismatch.
marta: query: `sum(rate(kv_prefix_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_prefix_lookups[5m])) by (region)` — this is post-deploy. Also saw a ~30% increase in token latency for short prefix path in EU.
sam: any change in cache keying? earlier we moved from prompt_hash -> model:prompt_prefix_hash for multi-model routing. Could that have changed collision rates regionally?
marta: key format unchanged in code, but we flipped on per-region splay window. The splay config now appends `:splay=<region-bit>` to the key for local replicas, which might block cross-region reuse.
kai: that splay change was intended to avoid KV NS hot shards — but if regions can no longer reuse cached prefixes when routing falls back, hit-rate gap makes sense.
perf-bot: perf-alert: eu-prefix-miss-rate increased 2.8x after deploy 2026-03-15T09:03Z.
deepa: ok hypothesis: splay reduces cross-region coherence and combined with routing policy we've been doing (weighted routing prefers US) causes EU/APAC to see mostly cold misses.
igor: what about replication? are we async replicating prefix writes across regions? I thought replication was best-effort.
marta: replication is eventual — async push on write. but write rate for prefixes is dominated by short-lived sessions; many prefixes only ever appear in one region. replication lag looks small (<200ms) but if we splay keys per-region, replication writes go to a different key.
sam: so current splay scheme creates distinct keys per region -> replication doesn't make them shared. That explains big hit-rate divergence.
kai: quick mitigation options: 1) remove splay suffix for prefix keys, 2) change routing to prefer local reads but allow cross-region read fallback, 3) synthetic warmup of popular prefixes in cold regions via traffic mirroring.
deepa: we should also re-run the kernel/batch combo in canary with splay toggled off to isolate impact. can we roll a short patch?
marta: I'm +1 on toggling splay off for prefix keys as an experiment. Patch ready:
```
# config snippet
cache.keying.prefixes: "model:${model}:prompt_hash:${p_hash}"
cache.splay.enabled: false  # toggle per-key-type
routing.fallback.read_cross_region: true
```
igor: timeline? we should canary to eu and ap-south only.
marta: canary starts in 10m if CI clears. deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary to eu-west & ap-south in 10m.
deploy-bot: canary started (eu-west, ap-south).
perf-bot: note — compare pre/post: track `kv_prefix_hit_rate`, `prefix_write_replication_lag`, `token_p50_short`.
kai: also add a short-lived background replicator that mirrors top-1000 prefixes across regions after each hour to warm cold caches while we iterate. cheaper than immediate global replication.
sam: any concerns about cost / consistency? mirroring duplicates keys (no splay) but it's a background async job, eventual consistency but improves availability.
deepa: let's do the canary. if EU hit-rate improves back to ~45-50% and token latency drops we'll promote. If not, revert batching tweak as fallback.
marta: canary results after 18m: eu hit-rate -> 44% (from 18%), apac -> 21% (from 7%), token p50 short down 28%. replication_lag unchanged.
igor: nice. implies keying/splay was main culprit, not kernel or batching.
kai: follow-up: design doc to propose per-key splay only for heavy-hot shards, and automatic cross-region shadowing of hot prefixes. Include estimated cost.
deepa: I'll open an RFC and link perf graphs. also add a short test that asserts that prefix keys are equal across regions unless splay flag set.
sam: any perf regressions still outstanding? we should watch kernel selector telemetry separately — low-level perf still had a small 4% CPU increase on long-seq tails.
marta: noted, I'll split the kernel change into another canary and run microbenchmarks. For now rolling the splay flag off globally for prefixes.
perf-bot: deploy success: splay toggle off promoted to prod after successful canary. monitor for 2h. :thumbsup:
igor: thanks all. learned: per-region keying is powerful for hot-shard avoidance but can catastrophically fragment cache for prefix reuse workloads.
kai: agree — need smarter heuristics: splay when write-density > X or when a prefix exceeds per-node request QPS. otherwise prefer global key.
deepa: RFC in #eng-runtime/rfcs by EOD.
marta: closing loop — will submit postmortem notes and add automated canary checks for prefix hit-rate divergence.
